newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia plans two more Eurobonds this year.
newsitem.headline: Russia plans two more Eurobonds this year.

text.p: Russia plans to issue two more Eurobonds this year, raising at least $2.0 billion, Finance Minister Alexander Livshits said on Friday.
At least one of the issues will be denominated in U.S. dollars, he told a news conference a day after the successful launch of Russia's first mark Eurobond.
The mark Eurobond raised two billion marks, and followed Russia's successful debut $1 billion offering last November.
"This year we are planning two more placements. The initial minimum volume is $2 billion," Livshits said.
"One issue will be dollar-denominated," he said, adding no decision had yet been taken on the denomination of the other Eurobond.

Livshits said Russia would also issue rouble paper next year alongside its dollar and mark Eurobonds, but it was not immediately clear whether he was talking of the creation of a rouble Eurobond sector. The rouble is not yet fully convertible.
"We shall issue rouble paper and it will be sold as well as the dollar paper," he said.
The Finance Ministry already regularly issues rouble-denominated Treasury bills and government bonds, which non-residents can buy and trade.
